analysis: Hepatic hemangiomas are benign liver tumors that are often asymptomatic and typically do not require treatment unless they become symptomatic or complications arise. The most common diagnostic approach is imaging, with MRI being particularly useful due to its high sensitivity and ability to provide detailed characterization of the lesion. Surgical intervention is not routinely recommended unless the hemangioma is symptomatic or causing complications, and percutaneous biopsy is generally avoided due to the risk of bleeding. Kasabach-Merritt syndrome, while associated with large hemangiomas, is rare in hepatic hemangiomas.
